headline: Bluefin: fish the cool south edge early, beat the afternoon SCA
body:
Today first, and mind the clock: a small-craft advisory hits the channel and outer waters from 3 PM through tonight, so this is a morning game — be on the fish early and headed in before the wind fills. The triangle at 37 nm reads calm at dawn, seas near 3 ft, winds only a couple of knots through midday before jumping to the mid-teens by 3 PM. Tuesday looks similar out there but a touch lumpier at 3.3 ft with wind up earlier, so today is the better window.

The break: all three corners run warm — west 71.4, east 71.5 — but the south point over the Basin is coolest at 69.4. The 64–68 band itself has slid off the south edge toward Santa Rosa Flats, and the Flats are unfishable — 15 to 20 kn, 4-plus-foot seas under the advisory. Don't make that run, and skip the longer Osborn and San Nicolas legs; both sit on warm side of the break anyway. Start on the south edge, on the coolest water you can find, and grind toward it.
